chunks: And among what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maymūn al-Qaddāḥ, from Jaʿfar, from his father, that ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say:

Whoever misses fasting the three days during hajj—and they are the day before al-Tarwiyah, the Day of al-Tarwiyah, and the Day of ʿArafah—then let him fast during the Days of al-Tashrīq, for permission has been granted to him.

These two reports have come as anomalous, opposing the rest of the reports, and it is not permissible to adopt them and abandon the many hadiths except by a proof that removes excuse. It is possible that the two men were mistaken in attributing that to Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, and that they heard it from someone else who ascribed himself to the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام, because it has been narrated that this was something ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥasan used to say, so they attributed it to him by mistake. Moreover, even if these two reports opposed the many earlier reports and those reports did not possess the advantage of greater number over them, it would still be necessary to set all of them aside and turn to what Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام narrated, because his narration has a manifest advantage over the narration of others due to his 'ismah, purity, integrity, and freedom from error.

key_terms.أَيَّامَ التَّشْرِيقِ: the Days of al-Tashrīq, discussed here as the time mentioned in the anomalous report
key_terms.الصِّيَامُ: fasting, specifically the required three days during hajj
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: the transmitted reports used for legal determination
key_terms.الْأَوْهَامِ: errors or misattributions from which the Imam is declared free
key_terms.الْحَجِّ: the pilgrimage context in which this fasting ruling applies
key_terms.الْخَبَرَانِ: the two reports under discussion and critique
key_terms.شَاذَّيْنِ: anomalous; describing reports that oppose the established body of narrations
key_terms.عِصْمَتِهِ: his infallibility, cited as a reason for preferring the Imam’s narration

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on someone who misses the three fasting days in hajj, and how are conflicting hadiths evaluated?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the ruling regarding one who missed the three prescribed fasting days during hajj and cites a report permitting fasting during the Days of al-Tashrīq. It then rejects that report as anomalous in light of more numerous narrations and affirms preference for the narration of Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام because of the manifest authority of the Imam.
